title: World Cities Report 2026: Urban Futures Beyond the Megacity
key_claim: Secondary cities (1-5M population) are growing 2-3x faster than megacities (10M+) in both advanced and emerging economies for the first time since 1990s.
notes: Anchor for the secondary-city-growth claim and the global-pattern framing.

title: Urbanisation and Climate Adaptation Finance Review 2026
key_claim: Megacity climate-adaptation financing gap projected at $1.5tn cumulative through 2035 against current commitments under $400bn.
notes: Anchor for the climate-adaptation cost burden on megacities.

title: Energy and AI Outlook 2026
key_claim: AI data centre electricity demand to reach 945 TWh by 2030; secondary cities with surplus generation and water capacity capturing 60%+ of new data centre capacity globally.

title: State of Metropolitan America Q1 2026: The Secondary-Metro Decade
key_claim: US secondary metros (1-5M population) captured 68% of net domestic migration in 2024-25; megacities (10M+) net-negative for the third consecutive year.
notes: US-specific data anchor for population-tilt claim.

title: Cities of the Next Decade: Capital Flows and Corporate Location Strategy
key_claim: Corporate regional-HQ relocations from megacities to secondary cities tracked at 14% annual growth rate 2024-26 across S&P 500 and Stoxx 600 firms.

title: Global Municipal Credit Outlook 2026: Climate Adaptation as a Binding Constraint
key_claim: Megacity municipal credit spreads widening 25-40 bps against secondary-city peers; climate adaptation cost burden cited as primary differentiator in 2026 ratings methodology.
notes: Anchor for muni-credit-divergence claim; key for investor-relevance section.

title: Multinationals shift regional HQs from megacities to second-tier hubs
key_claim: Named multinational regional-HQ relocations 2024-26 include moves from London to Manchester, New York to Austin, Tokyo to Fukuoka, Mumbai to Pune, Seoul to Daejeon.
notes: Landed-on-the-ground signal for the corporate location dynamic.
